newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin refuses big employment premium cut.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin refuses big employment premium cut.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin rejected on Thursday the suggestion of a major cut in unemployment insurance premia.

Currently employees pay C$2.95 per C$100 of insurable earnings. Asked if he supported the Canadian Chamber of Commerce's request for a reduction of 60 cents to C$2.35, he told reporters: "Sixty cents represents C$4 billion. We're certainly not in a position to do that."
The government is currently budgeting for a cut to C$2.90 in 1997 -- a five-cent cut that Martin said would cost C$350 million.

Martin did not respond when a reporter noted that he had announced on Wednesday that the government had undershot its 1995/96 deficit target by approximately C$4 billion -- the same amount that it would cost for a 60-cent unemployment insurance premium cut.
Employers pay 1.4 times the rate employees pay into the insurance fund.
Conservative Party leader Jean Charest last month called for a halving in the surplus in the unemployment insurance fund.
